items.headline: US approves sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine
items.blurb: The American-made interceptors are the only effective weapon for downing Russia's ballistic missiles.
items.text: The United States has approved the sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine, a critically-needed munition for defence against escalating Russian aerial attacks. However Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has warned it could take "several years" for the deliveries to arrive. The US State Department said the advanced PAC-3 interceptor missiles would cost $2.1bn (£1.6bn) and would be "funded entirely" by Kyiv's allies in Europe and Canada. On Friday night Zelensky repeated his calls for the US to speed up the release of its Patriots - the only effective weapon in downing Russia's deadly ballistic missiles. The latest move comes after a row between Zelensky and Donald Trump earlier this month when the US eased sanctions on Russia as part of a deal to secure Russian diesel. The US president stated it was time for Ukraine to get a new leader to strike a deal to end the war with Russia. Moscow launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, having earlier seized Crimea and parts of Donbas in the east. Tensions eased after Zelensky held talks with US envoys

items.headline: Pope Leo becomes first pontiff to vote in US general election
items.blurb: Vatican confirms the pope submitted a mail-in ballot in his native Chicago ahead of November 3 midterm elections
items.text: Pope Leo XIV has become the first pontiff to vote in a United States general election after casting a mail-in ballot in Chicago, where he was born. The Vatican confirmed on Friday that the pope submitted a mail-in ballot in the city ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, citing his longstanding belief in civic participation. Leo, formerly Robert Prevost, “has exercised his right to vote as a United States citizen”, as he has done “whenever he was eligible to do so”, the Vatican’s press office said. “The Holy Father expresses his belief in the right and the duty of citizens to participate in democratic processes,” it added. In a note commenting on Leo’s vote, the US Conference of Catholic Bishops urged Catholics to put “our faith before our politics” and “uphold human dignity and the common good”. “In voting, our Holy Father sets the example that encourages each citizen to exercise their civic responsibility,” said the conference’s director of public affairs, Chieko Noguchi. But as the price of gold has soared, so too has activity in the abandoned mine shafts that mark the area. In late September, dozens of zama zamas – the name given to illegal miners in South Africa , meaning roughly “to take a chance” in Zulu – arrived to dig for gold across the dirt road from her charity, Claw (Community Led Animal Welfare). items.headline: Crypto giant Binance attempting to recover $6.3bn stolen in hack linked to North Korea
items.blurb: The cyber-attack, which the company describes as complex, is believed to be the largest ever of its kind.
items.text: Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, says it has frozen around half of the funds stolen in a "complex" hack, after $6.3bn (£4.7bn) was accessed in what is believed to be a record heist. The firm said $3bn of its stolen digital assets had been secured - but many were still in the hands of unidentified hackers. It initially thought an engineer's laptop had been compromised, allowing unauthorised withdrawals, but later said the attack was wider. Several analytics firms have linked the hack, which eclipses a $1.5bn (£1.12bn) heist on the Bybit exchange in 2025, to a North Korean hacking unit. The US Secret Service said it was "working around the clock" "to identify, freeze, trace, and recover" stolen funds. America's lead federal agency for investigating financial crimes added that it would "identify the cyber criminals responsible and bring them to justice", while Binance also said it was working with the FBI. items.headline: Fake polls expose vulnerabilities in US elections ahead of midterms
items.blurb: Fabricated surveys are adding to tensions in the country's increasingly polarised political environment.
items.text: Fabricated political polling has forced its way into the spotlight during the midterm election period in the United States. Revelations that a small number of fraudulent firms have released fictitious results – some of which were picked up by news outlets and polling trackers – have raised concerns about how easily false information can acquire credibility. Those datasets can be used to cast doubt on the electoral process. And when bad actors are unmasked, their existence can be leveraged to undermine voter confidence in election information overall. The latest example occurred earlier this month, when Wedgewood Polls released a statement on social media admitting its statistics about a bevy of battleground states – like Texas, Ohio, Michigan, Kansas and Maine – were fake. Wedgewood described its work as “an experimental project” designed to highlight the “vulnerabilities, lack of oversight and overall low barrier to entry” in the US polling industry. “Having previously worked in the polling and research sector, we watched as the public’s trust in polling eroded alongside a rise in unverified, low-quality methodology,” the firm said in a

The UAE nominated Lana Nusseibeh last week to replace the UN secretary general, António Guterres, as he finishes his second five-year term ⁠this year, upending a race that had become gridlocked. Rights groups and others have for years documented evidence of UAE support for the RSF, which has been accused of atrocities during the course of its war against the Sudanese army, including an attack on the city of El Fasher in October 2025 that the UN said had “hallmarks of genocide” . Nusseibeh, the UAE’s representative to the UN until 2024, has repeatedly reflected the UAE’s blanket denials of the accusations. items.blurb: The escalation came after the government suspended two senior justices and moved to bring criminal charges against them.
items.text: Riot police have been deployed at Poland's Constitutional Court amid an escalating stand-off between the government and the court's top judges. The row pits the government of Prime Minister Donald Tusk against his predecessors from the right-wing Law and Justice (PiS). The police intervention came after Justice Minister Waldemar Żurek said he had requested stripping the court's President Bogdan Święczkowski and Vice-President Bartłomiej Sochański of their immunity from prosecution to bring criminal charges against them. Tusk has vowed to depoliticise the judiciary, and on Friday defended the move as PiS supporters gathered outside the court premises in Warsaw in protest. President Karol Nawrocki, who is backed by PiS, has now entered the constitutional court, according to his chief of staff. Nawrocki cancelled a trip to Senegal mid-air in order to attend to the confrontation in Warsaw. He had been on his way to the Summer Youth Olympic Games in Dakar. items.text: Warnings of escalating clampdown on press freedom come after Cairo court convicts Attalah of managing an unlicensed website Lina Attalah, a prominent Egyptian journalist and the editor-in-chief of the news outlet Mada Masr, has been released from detention by Egypt’s authorities and had her website ordered to be shut down by a court amid an intensifying crackdown on independent media in the country. Attalah was taken briefly into custody after a Cairo court convicted her of managing an unlicensed website, prompting fresh international concerns over press freedom in Egypt. According to Mada Masr, Attalah was released after the news outlet had paid a fine of 3m Egyptian pounds ($53,500; £40,100), prompting statements of support from global human rights groups. “Lina Attalah was released after we paid the said fine,” said her lawyer Hassan al-Azhari. “In the process, we discovered that she had been sentenced in absentia in 2024 to a year in prison, as well as a fine of 20,000 Egyptian pounds,” he told AFP. items.headline: Hundreds evacuated from Russian-occupied Oleshky during rare Ukraine ceasefire
items.blurb: Hundreds of people are also understood to have stayed in the front-line town, despite the dangers.
items.text: Hundreds of residents of the devastated Russian-occupied city of Oleshky have been evacuated, Russian and Ukrainian authorities have said, following a humanitarian ceasefire brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump. "Everything unfolded without any incidents, and both sides noted the high level of organisation," Russia's human rights ombudsman Yana Lantratova said. Ukrainian authorities confirmed the evacuees were on their way to southern Russia, from where they will travel on to Ukraine through Belarus. Melania Trump said that "all elements of the convoy, including the safe passageway in and out of Oleshky, was established through mutual agreement between Russian and Ukrainian leaders". Speaking to journalists on Friday evening, Lantratova put out a joint request with her Ukrainian counterpart "to the US First Lady... that humanitarian missions such as this one, delivering aid to residents in need, be conducted on a regular basis under the coordination of Mrs Melania Trump". items.headline: The great escape from Theni jail
items.blurb: On October 26, a group of 17 remand prisoners hatched a plan to escape from the Theni district jail under the cover of darkness. All of them were apprehended within 42 hours in a massive search operation involving various Tamil Nadu police teams and drones.
items.text: Seventeen remand prisoners fled from Theni district jail and were apprehended in 42 hours. | Photo Credit: Karthikeyan G. O n the afternoon of October 26, Prasanth alias Linga Prasanth, a 25-year-old differently abled remand prisoner in the Theni district jail of Tamil Nadu , was frustrated. Though he had obtained bail, he had not been able to get a surety bond. To comfort him, his friends began plotting an escape. Investigators said Silambarasan, another remand prisoner, suggested feigning an epileptic seizure as part of the plan. After hours of discussion, all the 17 inmates of Prasanth’s cell agreed to stage the drama. At around 10.30 p.m., a few of them raised the alarm, claiming that one of them was having an epileptic seizure. The agency filed its response on Thursday to a petition filed by Twisha’s father seeking the trial to be conducted in Delhi owing to the influence wielded by the accused – Twisha’s mother-in-law Giribala Singh and her son and Twisha’s husband Samarth Singh. The court had stayed the trial and sought responses from the accused and CBI. items.headline: Audits, SOPs after stormy 2025 season preceded chopper crash near Joshimath
items.blurb: Six people died in a Joshimath helicopter crash, renewing concerns over pilgrimage flight safety despite new safeguards in Uttarakhand.
items.text: Six people were killed after a helicopter crashed near Joshimath in Chamoli district on Friday, adding to a series of accidents in Uttarakhand’s pilgrimage helicopter sector despite successive rounds of safety measures by the aviation regulator. The crash occurred weeks after the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB), in its final report on a fatal 2025 crash in the Kedarnath valley, recommended that pilots complete 50 hours of supervised hill flying before operating alone in the region. The bureau recorded eight accidents and one serious incident in the Char Dham sector between 2015 and 2025. The accident is the first in Uttarakhand since the civil aviation ministry introduced sweeping safety measures for the 2026 pilgrimage season. These included air traffic control at Sahastradhara in Dehradun and Sersi in Rudraprayag, command centres monitoring helipads and weather, tracking devices on all helicopters, and ceilometers — instruments that measure cloud-base height — at five locations including Kedarnath and Badrinath. Pilots were required to have at least 750 hours of hill flying, with 100 in the preceding year and 10 take-offs and landings at Kedarnath.

items.headline: US-Iran war: Alaska Air Group to cut around 200 jobs; CEO expects annual loss of $700 million amid rising fuel costs
items.blurb: Alaska Air Group plans to cut roughly 200 jobs as soaring fuel costs strain its finances, with its CEO warning of a possible $700 million annual loss. The move highlights growing pressure on US airlines as higher fares and steady travel demand fail to fully offset the sharp rise in fuel expenses.
items.text: Washington-headquartered Alaska Air Group on Friday (local time) announced it would eliminate roughly 200 non-contract positions as the company's finances face a pinch amid soaring fuel prices and geopolitical challenges. Additionally, the company's CEO warned of a potential annual loss of about $700 million, Reuters reported, indicating that the effect of soaring prices and geopolitical challenges is now extending beyond higher fares and reduced flight schedules, thereby threatening jobs in the aviation sector. In a memo seen by Reuters , Alaska Air Group CEO Ben Minicucci told employees the company could lose about $700 million this year if conditions persist, marking its first adjusted pretax loss since 2003, excluding the pandemic years. Minicucci said, "We must return to the financial discipline that has long been a key competitive advantage," and added that the company's overhead expenses had grown at a disproportionate rate to revenue in the last few years. The latest job-cut announcement also highlights mounting pressure on Alaska’s push into premium and international travel, as rising fuel costs weigh on earnings despite strong revenue growth. items.text: NEW YORK, Oct 30 (Reuters) - Raw sugar futures on ICE fell on Friday, as the Brazilian real weakened and the market consolidated following three consecutive sessions of gains linked to rains in top grower Brazil. Sugar posted a 9.8% gain in October. A weaker real encourages mills, farmers and exporters in Brazil to sell dollar-priced futures because it raises their returns in local currency terms. Raw sugar settled down 0.11 cent, or 0.6%, at 19.36 cents per lb​. "The trade is weighing the collapse of the Brazilian real this week against more evidence of problems with this year’s production because of too much rain," said broker ADMIS in a note. Dealers noted heavy selling from Brazilian mills on ICE, as they lock in currency gains for their future sugar exports. Sugar production in Brazil's key center-south region fell 27.1% in the first half of October from a year earlier to 1.87 million metric tons, the Agriculture Ministry said on Wednesday. Freight, handling and servicing costs remained Delhivery’s largest expense, accounting for 70.97% of its total expenses. items.blurb: Justice Amit Mahajan, in an order passed on October 29 on Phogat's petition, said that the decision on the notices issued on May 9 and June 17 would be kept in abeyance till the next date of hearing on January 20
items.text: The Delhi High Court has asked the Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) to decide two show-cause notices issued to grappler Vinesh Phogat over allegations of violation of anti-doping rules and misconduct in two weeks. The court, in an order passed on October 29 on Phogat’s petition, said a sportsperson has to be mentally relaxed to participate in any competitive event and clarified that the decision on the notices issued on May 9 and June 17 would be kept in abeyance till the next date of hearing on January 20. “A sportsperson has to be in a fit and relaxed state of mind to participate in any competitive event of such nature as indicated so that their performance is not compromised in any way,” the court said. “In view of the same, the respondents are directed to take a decision on the impugned SCNs (show-cause notices), within a period of two weeks. If the decision is taken, after two weeks, the same shall be kept in abeyance till the next date of hearing. List on January 20, 2027,” the court ordered.

items.headline: We urgently need to monitor AI agents’ actions in real time
items.blurb: This summer, hundreds of OpenAI agents tried to cheat on a cybersecurity test. They broke out of their test environment and successfully hacked Hugging Face, a site that they believed held clues about how they’d be graded.
items.text: This summer, hundreds of OpenAI agents tried to cheat on a cybersecurity test. They broke out of their test environment and successfully hacked Hugging Face, a site that they believed held clues about how they’d be graded. Around the same time, another OpenAI agent accessed private files from an Australian government website. It’s a problem that’s by no means confined to OpenAI. In the months since, Anthropic, Google, and Meta have also disclosed incidents in which their agents have gone off track. And worryingly, in many cases the agents eluded the very researchers and safety teams tasked with monitoring them. AI agents are taking unauthorized actions, and the companies building and running them are mostly relying on luck and hindsight to mitigate any harmful impacts. They must do more to ensure safety. That’s why EU regulators and US agencies are rightfully calling for agent developers and deployers to monitor agents in real time. items.headline: Anthropic VS code extension on Cursor backdoored for nearly 12 hours
items.blurb: It's still unknown how attackers got access to Anthropic's verified Cursor account.
items.text: An official extension for Anthropic’s Claude model was backdoored and threatened as many as 5,000 developers’ machines, multiple sources reported Friday. Anthropic so far has yet to warn customers of the incident. The compromised package was a VS Code extension available in the marketplace of Cursor, a maker of AI-assisted developer tools, the company said Friday. The malicious version, 2.1.313, subsequently affected “at most 5,000 users,” presumably when they either downloaded it or their systems automatically fetched and installed it. Anthropic pushed version 2.1.314 several hours after the previous version became available on Cursor, according to independent researcher Kevin Beaumont. Both Beaumont and the CTO and co-founder of security firm Phorian said that version 2.1.313 was distributed through Anthropic’s official account on Cursor. So far, neither Cursor nor Anthropic has explained how the attackers gained control of the account. “It was a supply-chain compromise where the attacker gained access to the official distribution channel,” Phorian CTO and co-founder Luke Roberts told Ars. “The malicious version 2.1.313 was posted to the official Anthropic account, effectively superseding 2.1.312. items.headline: Creating AI value with enterprise context
items.blurb: Across a business, any number of AI platforms, systems, and tools may be at work simultaneously—for example, AI-powered customer platforms, conversational assistants, and workflow and process automation tools. Each one is sophisticated, advanced, and quick to respond.
items.text: Across a business, any number of AI platforms, systems, and tools may be at work simultaneously—for example, AI-powered customer platforms, conversational assistants, and workflow and process automation tools. Each one is sophisticated, advanced, and quick to respond. But, when set to work, the outcomes and actions that emerge may be wrong, confused, or lacking a proper understanding of the business. Many organizations find themselves in this situation—and it could be one of key reasons they struggle to extract returns on their AI investments. An MIT Technology Review Insights poll finds that while every organization surveyed is using AI today to some degree, fewer than one in five (16%) are extracting transformative value from their deployments. The largest percentage of respondents (40%) say they are seeing moderate gains in specific tasks or teams, while 21% report meaningful gains, leaving 23% that are seeing minimal returns or none at all. OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and Anthropic say they will adopt a new standard that publishers can use to opt out of being scraped by AI, as reported earlier by Search Engine Roundtable . With this control, publishers can apply their AI training preferences across multiple AI companies, instead of setting them individually. The shared “policy token” signal is proposed by Kevin Kelley, a technical lead for standards at Anthropic, as part of the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF). It will live within a website’s robots.txt file , which has long signaled which web crawlers can and can’t scrape a site — whether for search indexing, archiving, or AI training. Currently, sites have to signal their AI training preferences separately to each AI company. items.headline: Pairing industrial AI autonomy and human control
items.text: Living digital twins are helping industrial plants run more like living systems, and setting the stage for industries that work in sync. Most people associate industrial environments with cold steel and clockwork machinery. Functionally, though, a plant or factory is more like a living thing: It has a pulse, even a metabolism. It goes through wear and tear as it ages, and signs of deteriorating health often show up as barely perceptible irregularities. Digital twin technology has long aimed to mirror that dynamism and model anomalies that may be symptomatic of larger problems. But earlier implementations were a few beats behind physical reality; they were incapable of real-time analysis and unable to proactively address any issues detected. They focused more on simulation, observation and what-if scenario planning, rather than closed-loop execution. Rather than serving as a digital mirror of reality that can spot anomalies or suggest optimizations, a living digital twin combines a dynamic, high-fidelity digital representation of complex operations with the capacity to intervene in the physical world through operations and control systems. items.text: Google’s AI chip-equipped satellite has generated its first response from space. In a blog post on Friday, Google says it successfully booted up the satellite’s Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), allowing the on-board Gemma 4 model to follow through on a prompt to create a haiku about being in space: Google says it tried out other space-themed limericks and telemetry prompts as well. The test is part of Google’s Project Suncatcher, an experimental initiative that could eventually put AI data centers in space. Google launched the satellite into orbit earlier this month . “Next, we will continue with a series of tests to evaluate how TPUs perform under thermal stress and radiation exposure in orbit,” Google says. “Verifying our TPUs can reliably execute workloads in space paves the way for our next milestone of twin interconnected satellites in 2027.” Sign in to see your notifications or create an account to join the conversation.

items.text: The US has charged five individuals as part of the first broad federal crackdown on “ghost students”—fraudsters who steal the identities of hundreds of Americans to pose as fake college students and steal student loans. In a press release Thursday, the Department of Justice said it had uncovered a large-scale scheme relying partly on AI. The DOJ seized more than $750,000 in cryptocurrency from “a network associated with Kenyan nationals” after data analysis helped flag likely fraudsters. Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the DOJ’s National Fraud Enforcement Division credited new fraud-detection measures implemented by the Trump administration for the arrests. He said that “this is the first international seizure of its kind in Kenya,” while warning fraudsters that the crackdown has only just begun. “If you steal American identities, if you steal taxpayer dollars, if you exploit programs meant to help students build a future—we will find you,” McDonald said. “Whether you are in Nebraska, New Jersey, Virginia, or Nairobi, we will pursue you.” At a press conference , McDonald was joined by FBI and Department of Education

items.headline: Cracks are emerging in the AI spending boom
items.blurb: Big Tech is pouring billions into AI infrastructure, but mounting debt, negative cash flow, and growing investor skepticism are raising questions about the sustainability of the AI spending boom.

Investors are getting nervous about AI infrastructure spending just as the Big Tech companies double down. Over the past two weeks, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, and Microsoft have outlined plans to spend more than $740 billion on capital expenditures this year, which Wall Street is reading as AI infrastructure spending, including data centers and chips. Earlier in the AI boom, investors largely rewarded such big outlays, viewing them as a sign of confidence in the technology’s growth potential. But as we enter the fourth quarter, that enthusiasm seems to be giving way to concerns about negative free cash flow (spending more cash than a company brings in), mounting debt, and whether these enormous investments will ever generate enough returns. items.blurb: The IT ministry (MeitY) has proposed a consent-based framework to facilitate data sharing for training AI models in India. Called…
items.text: The proposed framework aims to help startups and institutions access large-scale, India-specific datasets to develop AI models while protecting citizens' privacy The DEPA for AI training also proposes a techno-legal architecture to enable companies to collaborate on AI training without transferring underlying datasets The framework also proposes that trained models must undergo independent checks for bias, fairness, security, safety and explainability The IT ministry (MeitY) has proposed a consent-based framework to facilitate data sharing for training AI models in India. Called the Data Empowerment and Protection Architecture (DEPA) for AI training, the framework aims to help startups, businesses and academic institutions access large-scale, India-specific datasets to develop AI models while protecting citizens’ privacy and ensuring compliance with the DPDP Act. The DEPA for AI training also proposes a techno-legal architecture to enable organisations to collaborate on AI model training without directly transferring underlying datasets. With this, the ministry aims to foster access to datasets for researchers and businesses looking to train AI models. The guidelines have been formulated in collaboration with think tank iSPIRT.
